meta.description: Layer 0 policy flags — always-on contextual warnings activated by pipeline and user context

flags.title: SNAP Application Barrier + Work Rule
flags.message: Missouri requires in-person application at a Family Support Division (FSD) office for SNAP. Online applications are not available for initial enrollment. Missouri also enforces an 80-hour monthly work requirement for able-bodied adults without dependents (ABAWDs) aged 18-49. Failure to meet work requirements results in a 3-month benefit limit per 36-month period.
action_items: Locate nearest FSD office: mydss.mo.gov/food-assistance
Confirm work requirement exemptions (disability, pregnancy, caretaker status)
If ABAWD, document work hours or apply for exemption before 3-month limit

flags.title: MO HealthNet Renewal Churn Risk
flags.message: Missouri MO HealthNet (Medicaid) has a 12-month eligibility period with redetermination. Post-unwinding from the COVID continuous enrollment provision, Missouri has experienced significant renewal churn — eligible individuals losing coverage due to procedural failures (returned mail, missed deadlines). Track renewal dates proactively.
action_items: Verify current enrollment status at mydss.mo.gov
Update mailing address with MO DSS immediately if changed
Set 60-day advance reminder before renewal date
If terminated, request reinstatement within 90 days of adverse action
Contact MO HealthNet hotline: 573-751-2005

flags.title: Non-Citizen Medicaid Eligibility Restriction (Oct 1, 2026)
flags.message: Effective October 1, 2026, Missouri will end MO HealthNet coverage for non-citizens who currently qualify under federal emergency Medicaid or state-funded programs. This affects lawfully present immigrants, DACA recipients, and refugees whose coverage was extended under prior policy. Individuals must transition to alternative coverage before the cutoff date.
action_items: Identify current coverage type (emergency Medicaid, state-funded, federal match)
Explore ACA Marketplace plans at healthcare.gov (lawfully present immigrants qualify for subsidies)
Contact FQHC network for sliding-scale uninsured care (KC CARE: 816-753-5144, Samuel U Rodgers: 816-474-4920)
If refugee/asylee, contact MO Office of Refugee Administration: 573-751-3221
Document coverage transition timeline — apply for alternative before September 2026
flags.legal_basis: Missouri HB 2634 (2026); 8 USC §1611 (federal public benefits restriction)

flags.title: TANF Structural Insufficiency — Force Bundle Pairing
flags.message: Missouri TANF (Temporary Assistance) provides a maximum of $292/month for a family of 3 — one of the lowest benefit levels in the country and insufficient to cover basic needs. TANF alone cannot sustain a household. The engine must automatically pair TANF with supplemental programs.
action_items: Apply simultaneously for SNAP (food), MO HealthNet (healthcare), and LIHEAP (utilities)
Contact local Community Action Agency for emergency funds
Explore Harvesters (KC) or St. Louis Area Foodbank for immediate food assistance
If employed, verify EITC eligibility for tax credit

flags.title: No State Paid Family/Medical Leave
flags.message: Missouri has no state-mandated paid family or medical leave program. Workers must rely on unpaid federal FMLA (if employer has 50+ employees and worker has 12+ months tenure), employer-provided leave policies, or short-term disability insurance. This is a critical coverage gap for illness, childbirth, and caregiving situations.
action_items: Verify FMLA eligibility (50+ employees, 12+ months, 1,250+ hours worked)
Check employer's voluntary leave policy and short-term disability coverage
If no FMLA coverage, explore MO HealthNet for medical costs
Contact Legal Aid of Western Missouri (816-474-6750) for wrongful termination if fired for medical absence
Document all communications with employer about leave requests
flags.legal_basis: 29 USC §2601 (FMLA); Missouri has no state equivalent

flags.title: Cold Weather Rule Protection (Nov 1 – Mar 31)
flags.message: Missouri's Cold Weather Rule (4 CSR 240-13.055) prohibits gas and electric utilities from disconnecting residential heating service between November 1 and March 31 when the temperature is forecast to drop below 32°F within the next 24 hours. Customers must register with their utility and may be required to enter a payment plan. If disconnection occurs during a protected period, it may be illegal.
action_items: Contact utility provider immediately to register for Cold Weather Rule protection
If already disconnected during protected period, file complaint with Missouri PSC: 800-392-4211
Apply for LIHEAP heating assistance: 855-373-4636 or mydss.mo.gov
Contact local Community Action Agency for emergency utility funds
Document all disconnection notices with dates and temperatures

flags.title: Involuntary Hold: Missouri 96-Hour Hold
flags.message: MO involuntary psychiatric hold law: Missouri 96-Hour Hold. Statutory authority: Mo. Rev. Stat. § 632.305. Maximum initial hold duration: 96 hours. Legal standard: danger to self/others. A hearing must be held before the hold can be extended. The person has the right to counsel at the hearing.
action_items: Verify hold did not exceed 96 hours without court order
Confirm hearing was held within statutory timeframe
Check that patient rights notice was provided at admission
Verify physician certification was completed
Request complete hold documentation from facility

flags.title: Psychiatric Patient Rights
flags.message: Psychiatric patients in MO retain fundamental rights during hospitalization: right to communicate with persons outside the facility, right to receive and send mail, right to access legal counsel, right to refuse treatment (with limited exceptions), right to informed consent, right to access medical records, and right to file grievances. These rights cannot be restricted as a condition of treatment.
action_items: Verify patient rights notice was provided and signed
Check whether any rights were restricted and if proper procedures were followed
Document any communication restrictions imposed
Confirm access to legal counsel was not impeded

flags.title: Federal Restraint & Seclusion Limits
flags.message: Federal law (42 CFR § 482.13) sets strict limits on restraint and seclusion in MO: physician order required within 1 hour, face-to-face evaluation within 1 hour, continuous monitoring required, maximum 4 hours per order for adults (2 hours for ages 9-17, 1 hour for under 9), and restraint may only be used to protect the patient from harm — never as punishment, convenience, or retaliation.
action_items: Request restraint/seclusion logs for all episodes
Verify physician order was obtained within 1 hour
Check that face-to-face evaluation occurred within 1 hour
Confirm continuous monitoring was documented
Verify restraint was not used as punishment or convenience
Check for injuries during restraint episodes
legal_references: CMS State Operations Manual Appendix A

flags.title: Involuntary Psychiatric Hold Statute
flags.message: This state has specific statutes governing involuntary psychiatric holds. Know the time limits, hearing rights, and appeal procedures before they expire.

flags.title: Mental Health Patient Bill of Rights
flags.message: This state has a Patient Bill of Rights for mental health facilities. Facilities must inform patients of these rights upon admission.
flags.statute: Missouri Mental Health Patient Rights Act

flags.title: Discharge Planning Requirements
flags.message: This state requires facilities to create discharge plans with follow-up appointments, medication management, and community resource referrals.
flags.statute: Missouri Mental Health Discharge Planning Standards
